prs.title: fix: skip JSON pre-parsing for str union annotations in pre_parse_json

clusters.pick_reason: #3063 keys `_request_streams` with `str(message.id)`, which collapses distinct ids (e.g. int `1` and string `"1"`) into the same key — this can cause a false-positive 409 rejection between two legitimately different ids. #3221 replaces this with a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (prefixing `i:`/`s:`) that keeps int and string ids distinct, and it also explicitly guards against a request id colliding with the reserved `GET_STREAM_KEY` sentinel used for the standalone GET stream — an edge case #3063's approach doesn't address.

members.author: Zelys-DFKH
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: RequestResponder.cancel() in src/mcp/shared/session.py sends an inappropriate wire message when a request is cancelled — the pre-existing code sent an error response for cancellation, which server.py's own comment flags as producing a duplicate/spec-violating response ("responder.cancel() already sent an error response, so skip the duplicate"). Both PRs rewrite the same lines of cancel() (hunks at line ~141-148 of the same base session.py blob 243eef5ae6) to stop that erroneous send, but land on different fixes: #2493 removes the error-response send entirely (send nothing, adding the comment "per spec receivers must not send a response for a cancelled request") and updates the matching server.py comment/log; #2514 instead replaces it with sending a proper `notifications/cancelled` message (imports CancelledNotificationParams), scoped to timeout/caller-initiated cancellation. clusters.pick_reason: #3063 keys `_request_streams` with `str(message.id)`, which collapses distinct ids (e.g. int `1` and string `"1"`) into the same key — this can cause a false-positive 409 rejection between two legitimately different ids. #3221 replaces this with a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (prefixing `i:`/`s:`) that keeps int and string ids distinct, and it also explicitly guards against a request id colliding with the reserved `GET_STREAM_KEY` sentinel used for the standalone GET stream — an edge case #3063's approach doesn't address.
